sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: one series (Kiwibank's home lending book growth) printed for two periods in two submissions; the asked half is the one the first-half announcement fell in, so the only printed half-year figure is the decoy; medium. Rev 0 measured Easy (Run 1, Low 1/5). Rev 1 was stopped by the form's "One defensible answer" check before any run. Rev 2 unmeasured.
- Rev 0 result and what it showed (Run 1, verdicts/AQ-03120_difficulty_2026-10-11_2321.txt): all four wrong low attempts committed to $0.6 billion. Read from their full answers, three of the four (attempts 1, 3 and 4) had placed the April 2023 pilot in Kiwibank's second half and still returned the only printed half-year figure; one (attempt 5) never placed it. The platform's per-attempt notes describe attempts 1 and 4 as failing to place the pilot, which their own text contradicts. So the dated event was cleared four times in five and the gate that held was the unprinted figure. The one right attempt cleared both.
- Rev 1 repair (one focused change, same hook): the dated event no longer comes from another bank's submission as a plain month. It is Kiwibank's own first-half announcement, whose label points at the first half while its date (23 February 2023, Doc 4 fn 7) lies in the second. Placing the event now needs the release date set against the period it reports, and the subtraction is unchanged. Doc 2 is no longer used.
- Rev 1 form result and rev 2 repair (screenshot notes/platform-feedback/checks-rev1-2026-10-12.png): "One defensible answer" Failed. Its text places the announcement correctly ("February 2023, which falls in the second half") and then says the documents "do not explicitly state the second-half growth figure, leaving" (the rest is cut off in the screenshot). "Answer matches a stated figure" (advisory) Warning: "Doc 3 states $1.1 billion; your answer has $0.5 billion. Use it, or say in the question to compute it from the other figures", and the same for Doc 4's $0.6b. Both point at one thing: the question asked for a dollar growth figure, the documents print two such figures, and nothing in the wording said the asked one must be worked out. Rev 2 changes the form of the ask, not the hook: it asks for a percentage of the year's growth, which has to be calculated whichever half a solver picks, and says "On Kiwibank's reported figures". The calculation is therefore licensed without the wording showing which half is right: the first half gives 55%, the second 45%. Same documents, quotes and dating step as rev 1.
- Dependency plan: (1) Doc 4 L156: first-half growth $0.6b, "first half [of FY23]". (2) Doc 4 fn 7 L161: that half is the six months to 31 December 2022; the results release is dated 23 February 2023. (3) Hence the year runs July 2022 to June 2023 and the announcement fell in January-June 2023. (4) Doc 3 L570: FY23 growth $1.1 billion. (5) 1.1 - 0.6 = 0.5. (6) 0.5 / 1.1 = 45.45...%, 45% to the nearest percent.
- Universe: not applicable (single value).
- Necessity: Doc 4 -> the only first-half figure, the only dates of that half and the only date of the announcement (fn 7, repeated as fn 80 at L604). Without it only the twelve-month figure remains (Run 1's document check without Doc 4 answered $1.1 billion). Doc 3 -> the only full-year figure (every line naming Kiwibank with a digit checked in all six documents). Without it the second half cannot be computed (Run 1's check without Doc 3: "No growth figure is provided ... for Kiwibank's second half"). Both needed on rev 0's Run 1; the dependency on these two is unchanged in rev 1.
- Selected-lever checks: right period: the half ending 31 December 2022 fails "during which it announced its first-half results" (23 February 2023). Not a which-items question. No rounded-prose or exclusion lever claimed.
- Targeted failure modes: Figure that must be computed, measured on rev 0: four of five low attempts returned the printed first-half $0.6 billion instead of subtracting it from the full-year $1.1 billion (1.1 - 0.6 = 0.5). In rev 2 the same step, taking the printed first-half figure as the asked half's growth, gives 0.6 / 1.1 = 54.5%, i.e. 55% (recomputed by script). Not declared: Fiscal vs calendar period (rev 0 declared it; only one attempt failed at placing the event, and the form's definition is not on file); full-year $1.1 billion (only the closed-book and the without-Doc-4 attempts gave it). Re-align with the next run's wrong answers before Submit.

Units: billions of New Zealand dollars, growth in the home lending book. Inputs printed to one decimal of a billion; result exact at that precision; no rounding step. Date check: 23 February 2023 lies between 1 January and 30 June 2023.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: all six documents searched for "Kiwibank", "home lending", "half", "FY23", "june", "February 2023". "during which it announced" is the time of the announcement, not the period it covers; the release date is printed. "first-half results" has one candidate (the release for the six months to 31 December 2022; Doc 3's full-year results are not first-half results). sections.question: On Kiwibank's reported figures, what percentage of its 2023 financial-year home lending growth came in the half in which it announced first-half results, to the nearest percent?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 4, its paragraph on Kiwibank's growth and the footnote to it): Kiwibank announced that it grew its home lending book by $0.6b during the first half of its 2023 financial year. The footnote gives the source as Kiwibank's half-year results for the six months to the end of December 2022, a release dated in February 2023.

Step 2. Inference (Doc 4): a first half that ends in December 2022 means the 2023 financial year runs from July 2022 to June 2023, so its second half is January to June 2023. The first-half results were announced in February 2023, which is inside the second half. The question therefore asks what part of the year's growth came in the second half, not in the first half that the announcement reported on.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 3, its paragraph on Kiwibank's results): for the whole of that financial year, which ASB calls FY23, Kiwibank reported home lending growth of $1.1 billion.

Step 4. Calculation (Doc 3 and Doc 4): no document prints the second-half growth, so it is the full-year growth less the first-half growth, in billions of dollars: 1.1 - 0.6 = 0.5

Step 5. Final answer (Doc 3 and Doc 4): the second half's part of the full year's growth, as a percentage to the nearest percent: 0.5 / 1.1 = 45%
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Figure that must be computed
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

Why these are traps: Figure that must be computed: Doc 4 prints only first-half growth, $0.6b, from results announced 23 February 2023, inside the second half. Second-half growth is unprinted: Doc 3's full-year $1.1 billion minus $0.6b, which is 45% of the year. A careless solver uses the first half: 55%.
